```{r}
# Exercise 1.1 - Question 2

# Create a numeric vector called x
x <- c(2, 9, 3, 8, 3)

# Multiply each value in x by 20
x * 20

# Perform arithmetic using order of operations
x + 4 * 24

# Multiply x by 10 and save the result as y
y <- x * 10

# Calculate the difference between the sums of x and y
sum(x) - sum(y)
```
```{r}
# Exercise 1.1 - Question 3

# Open the help file for ls()
?ls

# Open the help file for rm()
?rm

# The arguments for ls() are name, pos, envir, all.names, pattern, and sorted

# The sorted argument determines whether the results are sorted alphabetically
# TRUE sorts the results alphabetically, while FALSE does not request sorting
```

```{r}
# Exercise 1.2 - Question 7

# Assign the first flower's petal width to a new object
setosa1.petalwidth <- iris[1,4]

# Assign the first flower's petal length to a new object
setosa1.petallength <- iris[1,3]

# Display the petal width
setosa1.petalwidth

# Display the petal length
setosa1.petallength
```
```{r}
# Exercise 1.2 - Question 8

# Calculate the petal area by multiplying width and length
setosa1area2 <- setosa1.petalwidth *
setosa1.petallength

# Display the calculated petal area
setosa1area2
```
```{r}
# Exercise 1.2 - Question 9

# Calculate the petal area for each flower
# Save the results in a new column called PetalArea
iris$PetalArea <- iris$Petal.Length * iris$Petal.Width

# Display the first six rows to see the new column
head(iris)
```
```{r}
# Exercise 1.2 - Question 10

max(iris$Sepal.Length)
```
```{r}
# Exercise 1.2 - Question 11

# Calculate the average sepal length of all flowers
mean(iris$Sepal.Length)
```
```{r}
# Exercise 1.2 - Question 12
```

```{r}
# Exercise 1.3 - Question 1

# Create a logical vector containing three TRUEs and three FALSEs
a <- c(TRUE, TRUE, FALSE, FALSE, TRUE, FALSE)

# Display the logical vector
a
```
```{r}
# Exercise 1.3 - Question 2

# Find where the TRUE values are in my vector
which(a)

# Another way to find the same positions
which(a == TRUE)
```
```{r}
# Exercise 1.3 - Question 3

# Find where the FALSE values are
which(!a)

# Check the positions another way
which(a == FALSE)
```
```{r}
# Exercise 1.3 - Question 4

# Load the iris data again
data(iris)

# Count how many flowers have sepals shorter than 5.5 cm
sum(iris[,'Sepal.Length'] < 5.5)

# Check the number using which()
length(which(iris[,'Sepal.Length'] < 5.5))
```
```{r}
# Exercise 1.3 - Question 5

# Find the longest petal
max(iris[,'Petal.Length'])

# Find which flower has that length
which(iris[,'Petal.Length'] == max(iris[,'Petal.Length']))

# Check the petal width of that flower
iris[,'Petal.Width'][which(iris[,'Petal.Length'] == max(iris[,'Petal.Length']))]
```
```{r}
# Exercise 1.3 - Question 6

# Count how many flowers are versicolor
sum(iris[,'Species'] == 'versicolor')

# Check how many flowers belong to each species
table(iris[,'Species'])
```
```{r}
# Exercise 1.3 - Question 7

# Count the flowers with petals longer than 6 cm
sum(iris[,'Petal.Length'] > 6)
```
```{r}
# Exercise 1.3 - Question 8

# Find the species of flowers with sepals longer than 6 cm
iris[,'Species'][iris[,'Sepal.Length'] > 6]

# Another way to get the same species
iris[iris[,'Sepal.Length'] > 6, 'Species']
```
```{r}
# Exercise 1.3 - Question 9

# Count flowers with sepals shorter than 5 cm and wider than 3 cm
sum(iris[,'Sepal.Length'] < 5 & iris[,'Sepal.Width'] > 3)
```
```{r}
# Exercise 1.3 - Question 10

# Count flowers with petals narrower than 0.2 cm or shorter than 1.5 cm
sum(iris[,'Petal.Width'] < 0.2 | iris[,'Petal.Length'] < 1.5)
```
```{r}
# Exercise 1.3 - Question 11

# Find the average sepal width for setosa flowers with sepals longer than 5 cm
mean(iris$Sepal.Width[iris$Sepal.Length > 5 & iris$Species == "setosa"])
```
```{r}
# Exercise 1.3 - Question 12

# Find the longest petal length for virginica
max(iris[,'Petal.Length'][iris[,'Species']=='virginica'])

# Find the shortest petal length for virginica
min(iris[,'Petal.Length'][iris[,'Species']=='virginica'])

# Subtract the shortest length from the longest
max(iris[,'Petal.Length'][iris[,'Species']=='virginica']) - min(iris[,'Petal.Length'][iris[,'Species']=='virginica'])
```
```{r}
# Exercise 1.3 - Question 13

# Count the flowers with petals wider than 1 cm
sum(iris[,'Petal.Width'] > 1)

# Divide by the total number of flowers to find the proportion
sum(iris[,'Petal.Width'] > 1) / nrow(iris)
```
```{r}
# Exercise 1.3 - Question 14

# Make a new column and label all the sepals as long
iris[,'sepalCategory'] <- 'long'

# Change the label to short for sepals under 5.5 cm
iris[,'sepalCategory'][iris[,'Sepal.Length'] < 5.5] <- 'short'

# Count how many flowers are in each category
table(iris[,'sepalCategory'])
```
